property_summary: For every admissible initialize(...) input where _feeRate is <= 5000, the reference contract never reverts and after initialize completes feeRate == _feeRate; the mutant, which assigns feeRate before checking the cap, can transiently set feeRate to an out-of-range value causing observable difference when initialize is invoked with _feeRate > 5000 (mutant reverts but leaves feeRate set) — thus the invariant 'if initialize reverts then feeRate remains unchanged (zero)' holds for reference but can be violated by the mutant for some inputs.

For any call to initialize(...), if the call reverts then the contract's feeRate remains unchanged (i.e. still 0 for a fresh contract); the mutant can leave feeRate set even when initialize reverts, violating this invariant for some inputs.

For any inputs to initialize, if the call reverts then the contract's stored feeRate remains its pre-initialize value (fresh contract => 0); the mutant that assigns feeRate before checking the cap can leave feeRate changed despite revert, violating this rule for some fuzzed _feeRate > 5000.

For any fuzzed _feeRate and other initialize parameters, if initialize(...) reverts then the contract's public feeRate getter returns its pre-call value (for a fresh contract that is 0); the mutant that assigns feeRate before validating the cap can leave feeRate changed even when initialize reverts, violating this property for some inputs.

For any fuzzed initialize(...) inputs, if initialize completes successfully then c.feeRate() equals the provided _feeRate; the mutant (which assigns feeRate before validating the cap) can cause a revert on too-large _feeRate but nevertheless leave feeRate set (so there exists an input where initialize reverts yet feeRate != pre-call value), therefore the reference guarantees that a successful initialize sets feeRate to the argument and no partial assignment remains on revert while the mutant can violate that by leaving feeRate modified when initialize reverts.

For any input arguments, the first call to initialize(...) on a fresh C contract must succeed and set initialized == true; the mutant inverts the check causing initialize to revert on first call (or never set initialized), so for some inputs the mutant leaves initialized == false while the reference sets it true.

For any input parameters, the reference contract's first call to initialize(...) succeeds and results in c.initialized() == true; the mutant inverts the initialized check causing initialize to revert on first call and leave initialized == false for some inputs.

For any input parameters, calling initialize(...) on a fresh C contract should succeed (not revert) and leave initialized == true; the mutant inverts the initialized check causing initialize to revert on first call and therefore initialized remains false.
